The issue: `Container fluid` in `CustomAppShell.tsx:96` already stretches to 100% of the AppShell main area, and `Flex` renders as a block-level element that fills its parent's width by default. So `w="100%"` on the page-level `Flex` (`page.tsx:109`) is redundant — but redundant explicit width forces the browser to recompute an exact percentage-of-parent width on every reflow (including zoom-triggered ones), rather than letting it inherit naturally. At certain zoom levels this produces rounding/reflow glitches (extra horizontal scrollbar, content briefly clipped) that don't happen with implicit `width: auto`.

Other single-column pages in this codebase (`familytree/page.tsx`, `rules/page.tsx`) already omit `w="100%"` on their root `Flex` for this reason. `games/page.tsx` has the identical `Flex w="100%" direction="column"` pattern as this file.

# Run the project's mandatory finalisation checklist before reporting any task as done

## Steps

1. Run `npm run typecheck` and capture all output.
2. Run `npm run lint` and capture all output.
3. Run `npx knip` and capture all output.
4. If any of the three produced errors or warnings:
   - For lint issues — run `npm run lint:fix` first to auto-fix what it can, then re-run `npm run lint` to see what remains.
   - For knip findings — remove the unused files, exports, or dependencies it reports.
   - Fix **every** remaining issue — do not skip, suppress, or dismiss any output.
   - If you are unsure whether a problem existed before your changes, run `git stash`, repeat all three commands to establish a pre-change baseline, then `git stash pop` and fix only the new issues.
   - After fixing, re-run all three commands to confirm they are clean.
5. Repeat until all three commands exit with code 0 and report no errors or warnings.

## Done criterion

`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npx knip` all exit with code 0 and report no errors or warnings. Only then report the task as complete.

## Notes

- Fix issues in the order they appear — later errors are often caused by earlier ones.
- Avoid silencing a lint rule or adding a `@ts-ignore` / `eslint-disable` comment to make the output go away — fix the underlying problem. If a suppression is truly necessary (false positive, required vendor API), scope it as narrowly as possible (single line, specific rule) and add a short inline comment explaining why.
- If a typecheck error is in a generated file (`prisma/generated/`, `prisma/zod/`), do not edit it — regenerate it with `npx prisma generate` instead.

It might be a lot to ask, but what I want to mimic is the zoom behaviour of well-known sites such as https://www.bbc.co.uk/

That's less "one CSS tweak" and more "does the whole layout reflow instead of holding a fixed shape" — which is exactly what BBC does well: nothing has a hardcoded pixel width wider than it needs to be, horizontal groupings wrap instead of forcing a fixed row, and breakpoints are relative (em/rem) so they respond correctly when the browser's zoom shrinks the effective viewport. Mantine already gives you most of this for free (`Group` wraps by default, `SimpleGrid` takes responsive `cols`), so the real work is auditing components for the exceptions — fixed `w={px}`, flex children that can't shrink, tables without a scroll wrapper — rather than adding custom zoom-detection logic.

Fundamental question: is fluid the right choice for the container in the custom app shell?

Probably not, for most pages here — `fluid` means every page has to independently solve "don't get uncomfortably wide" and "don't overflow on narrow/zoomed viewports," which is exactly why you're seeing scattered redundant `w="100%"` props and unwrapped rows: there's no bounding parent doing that job once. BBC's actual pattern is a bounded, centered content column (roughly 1000-1300px) with full-bleed exceptions handled explicitly per-component, not a globally fluid container — switching to `Container size="xl"` (or similar) in `CustomAppShell.tsx:96` would centralize that and likely make several of the audit's findings moot.

The tradeoff: some of this app's content is genuinely data-dense (admin tables, results grids) and might want more than ~1300px on a wide monitor, so you'd want to confirm no page actually needs edge-to-edge width before making the shell-level change, or let specific pages opt out with their own unconstrained wrapper.

Want me to check whether any current page/component actually relies on full viewport width, then size a bounded `Container` accordingly?
Yes
